raw_response:
Let me think through this year on my 5 mu.

I have been doing wheat and maize on this land for twenty years. My husband works in the town some months, so the fields are mostly my job with my mother-in-law helping at busy times. Five mu is not big but it feeds us and gives some grain to sell.

**Wheat first (winter):**
Last year I got about 450 kg per mu from the wheat. Not bad. I will do the same thing — no reason to change when it worked. I plant improved seed, the kind the shop in town sells, "Jimai" something — I just ask for the same bag as last year. Traditional seed my mother used gave maybe 300 kg, so nobody here plants that anymore.

For the base fertilizer I buy two bags of compound fertilizer (15-15-15 or 18-18-18, whatever the shop has at good price) for each mu — that is about 40 kg per mu at planting. Then at spring green-up I spread urea, about one bag (50 kg) covers two mu, so 25 kg urea per mu. That gives me roughly 18-20 kg of nitrogen per mu total. My neighbor Wang's wife puts on a little more, she says more fertilizer more grain, but I cannot afford to throw money. Still, I would rather apply a bit extra than see yellow wheat — a bad harvest is a disaster.

Water: I irrigate three times. Once before winter so the ground freezes wet, once at jointing in spring, once when grain is filling. The well is mine to use so water cost is just the electricity.

Pesticide: I spray twice. Once for aphids in spring, once mixed with the foliar stuff for rust and the fly at heading time. Sometimes three times if the aphids come strong.

Tillage: After maize I use the rotary tiller — the village service comes with the machine, it is 50 yuan per mu, faster than ploughing.

**Maize next (summer, after wheat):**
I sow right after wheat harvest in June, no time to waste. I use hybrid seed — everyone does. Zhengdan or Xianyu type, whatever the dealer has fresh.

Fertilizer: one and a half bags of compound at sowing (about 30 kg/mu), then urea at big-trumpet stage, maybe 20 kg per mu. So nitrogen about 16-18 kg per mu. Maize does not need as much P as wheat I think.

Water: only once if the rains come normal, twice if July is dry. Last year we had drought so I watered twice. This year I will see.

Pesticide: once for the borer worm, sometimes twice if armyworm shows up.

Expected yield: maize does better than wheat, I usually get around 550-600 kg per mu.
